holidays.name: National Hot Mulled Cider Day
holidays.description: A day for warming your hands around a mug of spiced apple cider simmered with cinnamon sticks, cloves, and orange peel. It is the unofficial kickoff to cozy season, when your kitchen smells like autumn in a cup.
holidays.origin: A food holiday of the unofficial, internet-calendar variety, observed on September 30 to coincide with the chilly arrival of fall in the Northern Hemisphere. Its roots trace back to centuries-old traditions of mulling drinks with spices, which was a way to make drinks tastier and to keep warm in winter.
holidays.funFact: The word 'mulled' describes a drink that has been heated and spiced, and mulled wine dates back to at least the Roman Empire, when people warmed wine and added spices to improve its flavor.

holidays.name: International Podcast Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the audio medium that lets you learn about true crime, history, or the secret lives of ducks while doing the dishes. Listeners are encouraged to discover new shows and thank their favorite hosts.
holidays.origin: Launched in 2014 by podcasting fans and enthusiasts as a way to honor and promote podcasts worldwide. It is observed on September 30 each year and spread through social media and podcast communities.
holidays.funFact: The term 'podcast' was a blend of 'iPod' and 'broadcast,' coined by journalist Ben Hammersley in a 2004 newspaper article, even though podcasts do not require an iPod at all.

holidays.name: International Translation Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the translators and interpreters who help the world understand each other, from novels and treaties to the instructions on your furniture. It is a nod to the people who make 'lost in translation' a rare occurrence.
holidays.origin: Celebrated on the feast day of St. Jerome, the patron saint of translators, who translated most of the Bible into Latin. The International Federation of Translators has promoted the day since 1953, and the United Nations General Assembly formally recognized it in 2017.
holidays.funFact: St. Jerome is often depicted with a lion because of a legend in which he removed a thorn from a lion's paw, and the grateful lion became his loyal companion.

holidays.name: National Chewing Gum Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the humble stick of gum, perfect for freshening breath, passing nervous energy, or blowing giant bubbles that inevitably pop on your face.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday tied to the long history of chewing gum, which people have chewed in various forms for thousands of years. Modern gum took off in the 19th century with the use of chicle from the sapodilla tree.
holidays.funFact: Archaeologists have found 5,000-year-old chewed lumps of birch bark tar in Scandinavia with tooth impressions in them, making them some of the world's oldest known chewing gum.

holidays.name: Hot Mulled Cider Day Meets Ask a Stupid Question Day
holidays.description: A playful day that encourages curiosity by letting you ask the questions you were embarrassed to ask, like why the sky is blue or whether a hot dog is a sandwich. There are no wrong questions, only unasked ones.
holidays.origin: Ask a Stupid Question Day has been traditionally observed on September 28 in some calendars and on the last day of September in others, started by teachers who wanted to encourage students to speak up in class without fear of embarrassment.
holidays.funFact: Educators created the day on the idea that asking questions, even ones that seem silly, is how people learn, and many great scientific discoveries began with a question that sounded naive.
